remedies.description: Enforce IBAN format validation at the point of capture (frontend form validation) and add a backend schema check in the payment‑processing pipeline so malformed IBANs are rejected before submission.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: Can be implemented as a configuration or code change; no new tooling required.
remedies.residual_gap: None – the root cause (IBAN‑format refund failures) is eliminated; any remaining ticket volume would stem from other issues and is outside the scope of this remedy.

output.why_agent: Deterministic validation rules suffice; no LLM or iteration needed; no residual gaps; detection not required as remedy prevents malformed IBANs.

output.rationale: E-02 confirms IBAN format failures; H-PAYMENT-PROCESS-DELAY links processing errors to tickets; U-U1 asks whether these failures drive ticket volume. Monitoring ticket volume (ticket-db:response_times) and refund failures (payment-db:refund_failures) provides data to test U-U1. Improving FAQ addresses the release‑scope core feature to reduce ticket volume via self‑service (E-03 stakeholder request). Settlements status query is optional extra to verify downstream health. All queries are read‑only, posing minimal load and reversible; FAQ changes can be rolled back. Alternatives: rely solely on stakeholder interview (E-03) or implement a chatbot, but these do not address the confirmed root cause (IBAN errors) and would not satisfy success criteria SC‑SC1/SC‑SC2.

output.summary: IBAN format errors in payment processing cause refund failures (E-02) leading to refund-related ticket volume and perceived wait times (E-03). Evidence shows five refund records failing due to IBAN format (E-02) and ticket response time median is 2 hours under the 24‑hour SLA (E-01), indicating response times are not high. Stakeholder perception of long wait times (E-03) contradicts the data. Claims for a chatbot (CL-01, CL-02) reflect the perceived need. No release was made; the planned improvement to the self‑service FAQ (W-IMPROVE-SELF-SERVICE-FAQ) remains pending. The release was held because settlement status completeness is unknown, Layer 1 verification failed (completeness:settlement_status and semantic root‑problem alignment), and the bank‑api tool is unavailable.
